architecturalStandards.name: Practical product completeness (common-sense product reasoning)
architecturalStandards.summary: Pocket Studio must reason about the normal supporting behavior a requested capability implies (affordances, workflow continuity, state completeness, data lifecycle, validation, accessibility, permissions/consequences, product continuity, customer-perceived completeness) — not just literal requirement/component compliance. Every implied behavior is classified REQUIRED, CONVENTIONALLY_IMPLIED, RECOMMENDED, OPTIONAL, CONSEQUENTIAL_DECISION (never silently approved — surface via the Decision Ledger), UNSUPPORTED (represent truthfully), or UNRESOLVED (ask or record). See src/lib/generation/interaction-contracts.ts's module comment for the initial foundation.
architecturalStandards.firstVerticalProofTarget: Example App Ideas picker: selectable by mouse/keyboard/touch, populates and remains editable in its target input, survives the required lifecycle, verified by the Quality Gate, honestly reflected in Truth Status. Not deliverable until the Component Registry, Structured Renderer, generation pipeline, and Quality Gate exist — designated here for P2-EXIT or whichever unit first completes that pipeline.
architecturalStandards.status: foundation-laid, not complete — proportional extension required from each unit listed in appliesTo before that unit is considered done

completed: P2-01: Blueprint Engine — versioned/validated Blueprint model, deterministic generator from Product State/DNA/Requirements, structural validation (EV-0048, EV-0049, D-0019)
Phase 1 regression audit + fix: graceful failure on double-responding to a decision (EV-0050, D-0020) — forward-committed on top of the accepted phase-1-complete checkpoint, does not reopen Phase 1

Product Pattern and Interaction Contract System — closed vocabulary of interaction states + recognized product patterns, wired into the Blueprint Engine so every screen/workflow carries a required-states contract and validateBlueprint enforces it (EV-0051, D-0021)

Inference Boundaries clarification — per-state classification (required/conventionally_implied/consequential_decision) added to the Interaction Contract System; consequential states now surfaced in Blueprint.openDecisions rather than silently assumed approved (EV-0052, D-0022)

P2-02: Component Registry — closed set of the 29 Master Spec §26 UI primitives, Zod-validated recursive component-tree schema, unknown components fail safely (substituted with ErrorState + a reported warning) (EV-0053, EV-0054, D-0023)

P2-03: Build Planner — versioned Build Plan derived structurally from a project's latest Blueprint and Feasibility Report (phases, dependencies, screen order, component structure built from Component Registry primitives, navigation graph, data dependencies, backend/business logic, admin requirements, integrations, monetization, platform requirements, persistence, tests, acceptance criteria, evidence requirements, risk, blockers); planStatus is BLOCKED whenever the Blueprint is invalid, requests an unsafe/unrecognized capability, or has an unresolved consequential decision (EV-0055, EV-0056, D-0024)

P2-04: Generated-app data layer — GeneratedAppUser (a generated product's own project-scoped end-user identity, reusing the platform's password hashing) and GeneratedRecord (a generic {projectId, modelKey, data} store validated at write time against the project's current Blueprint dataModels) rather than dynamic per-customer schema migrations (EV-0057, EV-0058, D-0025)

P2-05: Structured Renderer + Interactive Runtime — component-renderer.tsx (real interactive DOM from a ComponentNode tree using only Component Registry primitives, native form actions, real Tabs/Modal/Drawer state), screen-data-binding.ts (pure List-node <-> real data/Loading/Empty/Error binding), render-runtime.ts (server-only read/write binding to the P2-04 data layer via the current Build Plan's dataDependencies) (EV-0059, EV-0060, D-0026)

P2-06: Full-stack generation orchestration — generateApplication() (single generation call: Blueprint -> Build Plan -> Truth Status sync to this project's real GENERATED/BLOCKED outcome), a live preview route at /org/[orgSlug]/[projectSlug]/preview/[screen] rendering real Build Plan component trees bound to real generated-app data, real generated-app-user credential verification (no session/cookie yet), verified end-to-end through an actual browser (EV-0061, EV-0062, D-0027)

P2-07: Demonstration product — closed the P2-06 placeholder-Form gap generically (Form Inputs now named after a bound data model's real fields, benefiting every product); ran Master Spec §54's exact required sentence through the full pipeline live in a browser and honestly documented the gap between §56's full 11-screen/11-data vision and today's actual deterministic output (Home/Browse only, zero data models) as a disclosed, not-silently-implied limitation (EV-0063, EV-0064, D-0028)

P2-08: Conversational editing, Change Sets, selective regeneration — new ChangeSet model (1:1 with its governing Decision) computing addedCategories by diffing requirements derived from the prior idea vs. the combined (never-discarded) idea text; edit_request intents now generate a Change Set and apply it immediately (non-consequential) or hold it PENDING until Decision approval (consequential); regeneration only happens when addedCategories is non-empty. Also fixed a real regression this work surfaced live in the e2e suite: generateProductIntelligence silently reset a customer's edited unitEconomicsAssumptions on a second call, since ProductState is full-replace — now carries that one customer-editable field forward (EV-0065, EV-0066, D-0029)

P2-09: Version history and restore — getProjectVersionHistory aggregates ProductState/Blueprint/BuildPlan/ChangeSet into one chronological, immutable-by-construction timeline; previewBlueprintRestore computes a real screens/dataModels diff; validateBlueprintRestore re-validates a target version's stored content before restoring; restoreBlueprintVersion creates a new top version with the target's content, never mutating history in between. Restore scoped to Blueprint only (Build Plan is cheaply regenerable; Product State restore has no established use case yet) (EV-0067, EV-0068, D-0030)

P2-10: Quality Gate for the generated product — runQualityGate() runs 8 real checks against a project's current Blueprint/Build Plan (structural validity, no blockers, well-formed Interaction Contracts, list-view screens actually data-bound, form-submission Inputs matching their bound data model's real fields, screen reachability, image alt text, and a real server-side data-binding smoke check), recording Product Evidence and syncing Truth Status for a new quality.gate subject key — never a self-report (EV-0069, EV-0070, D-0031)

P2-11: Security/privacy/governance impact + legal draft generation — GovernanceProfile fields (dataCategories, monetizationModel, relevantGovernanceDomains) and security/privacy requirements now derived entirely from a project's real Blueprint content (never guessing jurisdiction/location facts); Terms of Service/Privacy Policy/AI Disclosure drafts generated from real Blueprint/Product DNA state with facts §34 forbids inventing (company identity, jurisdiction, contact) left as bracketed placeholders + recorded Open Questions, never fabricated; every draft carries an explicit not-legal-advice/requires-professional-review notice. 10 of 13 PolicyDocumentType values still have no content generator (EV-0071, EV-0072, D-0032)

P2-12: Migration planning for generated-app data model changes — planDataModelMigration performs the full §28 sequence (schema diff, real data-loss analysis querying actual GeneratedRecord rows per removed field rather than guessing, compatibility notes, ordered migration plan, honest backup requirement disclosing no automated backup mechanism exists, rollback plan referencing P2-09's restore) between any two Blueprint versions; recordMigrationPlanDecision records it as CONSEQUENTIAL when destructive or ROUTINE otherwise, reusing the existing Decision Ledger. Standalone/explicitly-invoked, not wired into applyChangeSet's auto-apply path (EV-0073, EV-0074, D-0033)

P2-13: Export foundation + durable jobs — exportProject() bundles Product State/DNA/Blueprint/Build Plan/GeneratedRecords/generated-app users (allowlisted, never passwordHash)/policy drafts/GovernanceProfile/Truth Status into one structured JSON bundle with honest disclosures (not a deployable package, not a backup); new JobRun model (PENDING/RUNNING/SUCCEEDED/FAILED, checkpoint, idempotencyKey, attempt) wraps (never modifies) generateApplication via runGenerationJob — idempotent, retryable, real status for the first time. Checkpointing coarse-grained (before/after, not sub-steps) (EV-0075, EV-0076, D-0034)

knownLimitations: Blueprint generation (P2-01) is deterministic/template-based, keyed off the Requirements Engine's Impact Analysis categories — not real design intelligence. Every generated Blueprint discloses this via generationMetadata.generatedBy and generationMetadata.method. Real AI-backed generation is Phase 3 scope (§61).

Generation (P2-06) is live at /org/[orgSlug]/[projectSlug]/preview/[screen], but that route is gated by the existing Pocket-Studio-side platform session (requireUserForPage), not a separate unauthenticated end-user-facing route. authenticateGeneratedAppUser verifies real credentials but does not yet establish a session/cookie — GeneratedAppUser/GeneratedRecord still cannot be reached by an actual customer of the generated product, only by the builder previewing it.

Build Plan component trees remain minimal pattern-driven placeholders, not real designed layouts. (Form Input naming was fixed in P2-07 to match a bound data model's real fields, so a genuine field-matched submission now succeeds when a data model is bound — see D-0028.)

The official Phase 2 demonstration (P2-07, Master Spec §56: 'Build a premium booking app for mobile detailers.') runs successfully end to end (GENERATED, VALID, READY, live in a browser) but its honest current output is only the base Home/Browse screens with zero data models — far short of §56's full vision (11 customer screens, 11 owner screens, 11 data types: Services, Packages, Availability, Memberships, etc.). This gap is intentionally NOT closed by hardcoding this one sentence's content, per Master Spec §26's 'not hardcoded preview screens' requirement — closing it honestly requires either a deliberately expanded, reusable domain-template vocabulary or real AI-backed generation (Phase 3, §61). See official-demonstration.integration.test.ts's module comment for the full accounting.

Conversational editing (P2-08) 'selective regeneration' is category-level (regenerate the whole Blueprint/Build Plan, or don't), not screen/field-level — true incremental diffing of individual screens or data models does not exist yet.

Version history (P2-09) aggregates Product State/Blueprint/Build Plan/Change Set into one read-only timeline, and restore exists for Blueprint only — Build Plan and Product State have no restore function yet (Build Plan is cheaply regenerable from a Blueprint; Product State restore has no established use case). No Studio UI surface exists yet for browsing version history or triggering a restore (P2-17).

The Quality Gate (P2-10) runs 8 real structural/server-side checks but does not run a per-generation browser e2e test or live authorization/tenant fuzzing — tenant isolation is verified structurally (by construction, via P2-04's own tests), not re-tested per Quality Gate invocation. No Studio UI surface exists yet for viewing Quality Gate results (P2-17).

Legal draft generation (P2-11) only has real content generators for 3 of 13 PolicyDocumentType values (Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, AI Disclosure) — the other 10 (Acceptable Use Policy, Cookie Notice, subscription/cancellation terms, data-retention policy, support policy, accessibility statement, communications consent, mobile-permission explanations, marketplace terms) still have no content generator. No professional legal review workflow exists (Master Spec §34's publication requirement) — drafts are generated only, never marked reviewed or published. No Studio UI surface exists yet for viewing/generating these (P2-17).

Migration planning (P2-12) is a standalone, explicitly-invoked tool, not wired into applyChangeSet's auto-apply path — a Change Set that would be destructive to existing GeneratedRecord data still regenerates automatically today (P2-08's existing consequential-decision gate covers Impact Analysis categories, not data-loss risk specifically). No automated backup/snapshot mechanism exists for GeneratedRecord data — disclosed honestly by every migration plan and every export bundle rather than implemented.

Export (P2-13) produces a structured JSON bundle only — no real code-file/deployment export exists. Durable jobs (P2-13) only wrap the GENERATION operation, with coarse-grained (whole-call, not sub-step) checkpointing — no other long-running operation is a durable job yet, and there is no true step-by-step resumability if interrupted mid-generation. No Studio UI surface exists yet for triggering exports or viewing job status (P2-17).

The Build Planner's planStatus deliberately does not treat the platform's own SUPPORTED_LATER_PHASE generation capability as a blocker (see D-0024) — a Build Plan can be READY today even though nothing yet executes it; that gap is disclosed via Truth Status and this list, not via planStatus.
Blueprint has no Studio UI surface yet (P2-17 wires this up); it is currently reachable only via the service layer and its integration tests.

The Product Pattern and Interaction Contract System (src/lib/generation/interaction-contracts.ts) validates that an interaction contract is declared and structurally complete, not that a generated screen actually implements the required states — no component tree or renderer exists until the Structured Renderer (P2-05) and generation pipeline (P2-06). Pattern inference is a fixed, hand-authored deterministic mapping (5 patterns, 7 states), not semantic understanding.

The 'practical product completeness' standard (D-0022, AS-0001) is only partially implemented: per-state inference classification exists and consequential states are surfaced in Blueprint.openDecisions, but implied-requirement identification in Product Intelligence, explicit-vs-inferred recording throughout the full Blueprint, Build Planner conversion of behavior into implementation work, renderer implementation, workflow-derived generated tests, Quality Gate runtime verification, and Truth Status reporting of unverified behavior do not exist yet. P2-02's contribution to AS-0001 is structural only: the registry's own failure mode (unknown components fail safely, never silently) is itself a completeness behavior, and COMPONENT_CATEGORIES gives the Build Planner a structural vocabulary to reason with — but no per-component interaction-state contract (e.g. a Button's pressed/disabled states) exists yet; that is deferred to P2-05 (the renderer), per D-0023. P2-03's contribution to AS-0001: the Build Planner's `tests` facet is derived directly from each screen's Interaction Contract required states (not invented separately), and `blockers` treats an unresolved consequential decision as a hard blocker — but Build Planner cannot yet verify a generated implementation actually satisfies those states. P2-05's contribution to AS-0001: LoadingState/EmptyState/ErrorState are now real, working primitives genuinely swapped in by screen-data-binding.ts based on real data state — not just declared in an Interaction Contract — but nothing yet automatically verifies every screen a Build Plan produces actually wires its List to this binding (that requires the generation pipeline, P2-06, and a Quality Gate check, P2-10). The designated 'Example App Ideas' first vertical proof is not delivered — that UI pattern does not currently exist in the product, and proving it requires systems not yet built.

The Phase 1 regression audit (D-0020) was bounded, not exhaustive — it read every page in src/app for missing implied behavior but is not a substitute for a full UX review. It does not reopen or invalidate the accepted Phase 1 Level 3 review (round 2, EV-0047).
Every Phase 1 known limitation not resolved by Phase 2's scope still applies (see PHASE_1_COMPLETION_REPORT.md).
nextAction: Begin P2-14: Web and PWA output (Master Spec §39, §40). §39 requires tracking each output target (responsive web, PWA, iOS, Android) independently with its own status (requested/supported/planned/generated/implemented/tested/built/...), never treating completion on one target as evidence for another — today Blueprint.outputTargets is just a flat string array (['web']) with no independent status tracking at all, and the live preview route (P2-06) is a plain responsive page with no PWA manifest, service worker, or installability. Concretely: (1) an OutputTargetStatus concept giving 'web' and 'pwa' their own truthful status per project (reusing the existing TruthStatusEntry pattern/subjectKey convention rather than new schema where possible); (2) real PWA output — a generated manifest.json and minimal service worker for a project's live preview, honestly scoped (offline/push are explicitly 'where appropriate'/'where supported', not required); (3) explicit, customer-facing language distinguishing web, PWA, and native mobile output, per §40's explicit requirement to 'explain the difference.'
